findings.title: Insufficient balance for first depositor on Hub when rounding error is covered
findings.description: This vulnerability occurs when the HubPortal covers rounding errors from yield during a user's deposit, leading to a balance mismatch between the actual M token balance and the amount recorded for cross-chain transfer. The root cause is that the protocol returns the specified amount (including the rounding deficit) while the actual balance is lower, and this deficit is covered from yield. An attacker could exploit this by being the first depositor after deployment and triggering a transfer back to the Hub, which would fail due to insufficient balance. The impact is a denial-of-service (DoS) for the first depositor when a small rounding error occurs, preventing successful redemption of tokens.

findings.title: Missing whenNotPaused modifier allows sendEarnersMerkleRoot to operate during protocol pause
findings.description: The sendEarnersMerkleRoot function in HubPortal lacks the whenNotPaused modifier, allowing it to be called even when the protocol is paused. This inconsistency in access control creates a security gap where critical cross-chain messages (earner Merkle root updates) can still be sent during an emergency pause, unlike other message-sending functions which are properly restricted. The root cause is the omission of the modifier in both overloads of the function. An attacker or malicious actor could exploit this to force state updates across chains during a pause, potentially disrupting protocol recovery or synchronization. The impact is low, as it does not lead to fund loss but undermines the intended security posture of the pause mechanism.

findings.title: Missing hubChainId_ constructor parameter will not allow Spoke Portal upgrades
findings.description: The SpokePortal V2 upgrade function does not include the new hubChainId_ parameter in its constructor call, which is required by the new implementation. This omission prevents successful upgrades of SpokePortal contracts because the constructor expects this parameter. The root cause is an incomplete migration script that fails to pass all necessary arguments during deployment. An attacker cannot directly exploit this, but it results in a functional failure during upgrades, rendering the upgrade process ineffective. The impact is low, as it affects only upgradeability and not runtime security, but it could delay critical updates if not fixed.

findings.title: Missing crossSpokeTransferEnabled will not allow Spoke Portal upgrades
findings.description: The upgrade function for SpokePortal fails to include the crossSpokeTransferEnabled parameter in the initialize call, which is introduced in the V2 implementation. This causes the initialization to be incomplete, as the new state variable will not be properly set. The root cause is the omission of this parameter in the abi.encodeCall used during the upgrade process. This issue prevents the correct configuration of cross-spoke transfer functionality after an upgrade. The impact is low, as it does not lead to fund loss or direct exploitation, but it breaks intended functionality and could misconfigure the protocol state post-upgrade.
